### 2.3.2 Job Lifecycle Process Flow

The following flow is the process every feature participates in; it is the reference flowchart for §2.2's acceptance criteria and complements the component diagram in §1.2.2.2.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Caller: every n — F-001 / F-015"] --> Unit["Unit property sets Job.unit<br/>returns self"]
    Unit --> Refine["Optional refinement:<br/>weekday, at, to, until, tag"]
    Refine --> DoCall{"do func, args — F-007"}
    DoCall -->|"unit missing or invalid"| Reject["ScheduleValueError raised<br/>job NEVER appended — F-016"]
    DoCall -->|"valid"| Compute["_schedule_next_run<br/>interval, weekday, at_time, tz, jitter"]
    Compute --> Naive["Convert tz-aware result to<br/>naive local next_run — F-004"]
    Naive --> Register["scheduler.jobs.append job"]
    Register --> Poll["Caller invokes run_pending or run_all — F-009"]
    Poll --> Due{"should_run: now >= next_run?"}
    Due -->|"no"| Poll
    Due -->|"yes"| RunJob["Job.run — sorted by next_run"]
    RunJob --> Deadline{"Already past until deadline? — F-006"}
    Deadline -->|"yes"| Unschedule["Return CancelJob<br/>_run_job removes job — F-010"]
    Deadline -->|"no"| Invoke["Invoke job_func<br/>exceptions propagate uncaught"]
    Invoke --> Restamp["Set last_run, recompute next_run"]
    Restamp --> PostCheck{"New next_run past deadline<br/>or job returned CancelJob?"}
    PostCheck -->|"yes"| Unschedule
    PostCheck -->|"no"| Poll
```

### 2.3.3 Integration Points

| Integration point | Mechanism and evidence |
|---|---|
| Host control loop | The caller invokes `run_pending()` on its own cadence; `docs/examples.rst` shows both the fixed `sleep(1)` loop and the `idle_seconds()`-driven loop |
| Job callable boundary | `do()` binds an arbitrary callable via `functools.partial` (655) and `run()` invokes it with no exception guard (691) — `docs/exception-handling.rst` makes wrapping the caller's responsibility |
| Threading and background execution | Not provided by the library; `docs/background-execution.rst` supplies a caller-implemented `threading.Thread` + `threading.Event` pattern and `docs/parallel-execution.rst` a `queue.Queue` worker pattern |
| Logging pipeline | The host attaches handlers to the `schedule` logger and sets its level (`docs/logging.rst`); the library only emits records |
| Timezone data | `pytz` is resolved at `at()` call time (499); absent, a `ModuleNotFoundError` surfaces, which `docs/faq.rst` resolves with `pip install pytz` |
| Multi-tenant scheduling | Independent `Scheduler()` instances, each polled separately (`docs/multiple-schedulers.rst`) |
| Type tooling | `schedule/py.typed` plus inline annotations make the public surface visible to consumer type checkers; `setup.cfg` and `tox.ini` enforce `mypy -p schedule` |
| Packaging toolchain | setuptools ≥ 61 backend (`pyproject.toml`); wheel build and twine upload procedure in `docs/development.rst`; sdist contents controlled by `MANIFEST.in` |

There are no HTTP, RPC, CLI, message-broker, database, or filesystem integration points: the runtime module imports only the eight standard-library modules listed at `schedule/__init__.py` 41–48.

### 2.3.4 Shared Components

| Shared component | Location | Features that depend on it |
|---|---|---|
| `Scheduler.jobs` list — the single in-memory registry | 86–87 | F-007 (append), F-009 (iterate), F-010 (remove), F-011 (filter/clear), F-012 (min), F-015 (`jobs` alias) |
| `Job._schedule_next_run()` — the one next-run calculator | 700–748 | F-001, F-002, F-003, F-004, F-005 (jitter draw), F-006 (post-run deadline check), F-007 (first computation) |
| `Job.__lt__` — ordering by `next_run` | 257–262 | F-009 (`sorted()` execution order), F-012 (`min()` selection) |
| `Job._correct_utc_offset()` — offset/DST normalization | 773–817 | F-004 directly; F-003 indirectly through `_move_to_at_time` (769) |
| `Job._is_overdue()` — deadline comparison | 819–820 | F-006 (both pre- and post-execution checks), F-010 (produces the cancellation signal) |
| `CancelJob` sentinel | 71–76 | F-010 (recognition), F-006 (deadline expiry), caller code (`docs/examples.rst`, `docs/exception-handling.rst`) |
| Exception hierarchy | 53–68 | F-001…F-007 raise from it; F-016 defines it |
| `logger` — the module-wide `schedule` logger | 50 | F-009, F-010, F-011, F-014 |
| `Job` field set assigned in `__init__` | 227–255 | Every feature reads or writes a subset; it is the complete data model |
| Private weekday helpers `_move_to_next_weekday`, `_weekday_index` | 916–945 | F-002 (both), F-016 (`ScheduleValueError` for unknown days) |

### 2.3.5 Common Services

The module provides four internal services rather than external ones; each is used by multiple features.

| Common service | Implementation | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| Time source | `datetime.datetime.now()`, made zone-aware only when `at_time_zone` is set (717); `time.sleep` used solely for `run_all` spacing (120) | F-001, F-004, F-006, F-009, F-012 |
| Configuration validation | Interval, unit, format, timezone-type, range, and deadline guards raising the F-016 hierarchy | F-001, F-002, F-003, F-004, F-005, F-006, F-007 |
| Registry service | Append, copy, filter, slice-delete, and remove operations on `Scheduler.jobs` | F-007, F-009, F-010, F-011, F-012 |
| Diagnostics service | Lazy `%`-formatted DEBUG records on the `schedule` logger, rendering jobs through F-013 | F-009, F-010, F-011 |

Two services that a scheduler of this kind might be expected to share are demonstrably **absent**, and their absence is a documented design position rather than an omission: there is no persistence/serialization service (no file, database, or serialization call exists anywhere in the module) and no concurrency service (no threading, locking, queue, or async construct exists) — see `docs/index.rst` non-goals, `docs/parallel-execution.rst`, and `docs/background-execution.rst`.

## 2.4 Implementation Considerations

### 2.4.1 System-Wide Constraints Binding Every Feature

| Constraint | Statement and evidence |
|---|---|
| Naive-local datetime contract | `_schedule_next_run()` converts a timezone-aware result back to local time and strips `tzinfo`, with the inline comment stating the goal is API consistency with older versions (`schedule/__init__.py` 740–747). `docs/timezones.rst` publishes the same contract. Any feature that exposed aware datetimes would be a breaking change under the semantic-versioning policy declared in `docs/development.rst` |
| Zero required dependencies | `pyproject.toml` declares `dependencies = []`. New functionality may only use the standard library or a lazily imported optional extra — the pattern F-004 already follows at line 499 |
| Python 3.7 floor | `python_requires=">=3.7"` (`setup.py`) and `requires-python = ">= 3.7"` (`pyproject.toml`). Because the floor predates `zoneinfo` in the standard library, timezone support is built on `pytz`, and `Job.at()` accepts only `str` or `pytz.BaseTzInfo` (501–508) |
| Single-module architecture | The entire runtime is `schedule/__init__.py` (945 lines) plus the 0-byte `schedule/py.typed`. Every feature shares one namespace, one logger, and one import block, so cross-feature coupling must be managed by convention rather than module boundaries |
| Serial, caller-driven execution | `run_pending()` executes in-line on the calling thread (89–101). `docs/index.rst` states job duration is not accounted for, and `docs/parallel-execution.rst` records serial execution as a deliberate choice |
| Quality gates on every change | `tox.ini` runs `py.test … --cov schedule` and `mypy -p schedule` across twelve environments; `black --check .` (black pinned to `20.8b1`), `sphinx-build -W`, and `setup.py check --strict --metadata --restructuredtext` are separate gates, all wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for pushes and pull requests against `master` |
| Test determinism | `test_schedule.py` fixes the process timezone to a POSIX Berlin rule and calls `time.tzset()` (lines 23–30) and substitutes a controlled `datetime` subclass through the `mock_datetime` context manager (line 39). Any new time-dependent feature must be testable within that harness |
| Release ritual | `docs/development.rst` requires updating `HISTORY.rst` and `AUTHORS.rst`, bumping the version in **both** `setup.py` and `docs/conf.py`, tagging `X.Y.Z`, then building a wheel and uploading to TestPyPI followed by PyPI |

### 2.4.2 Per-Feature Technical Constraints

| Feature | Technical constraints |
|---|---|
| F-001 | Unit strings must remain valid `datetime.timedelta` keyword arguments (line 729), which fixes the vocabulary at seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks; unit accessors are properties, so they cannot take arguments |
| F-002 | Weekday scheduling is valid only for a weekly interval (`IntervalError` in all seven accessors, 380–455) and requires `unit == "weeks"` at scheduling time (721–724); day names are a fixed lowercase tuple (931–945) |
| F-003 | Three anchored regexes fix the accepted formats per unit (513, 518, 524); the daily pattern permits an hour of 20–29, so the explicit 0–23 bound at 544–549 is load-bearing and must be retained |
| F-004 | Timezone support exists only in `at()`; `pytz` must stay a lazy in-method import; `zoneinfo` objects are rejected by the type check; DST-gap resolution is explicitly a best effort ("schedule the job 1 offset later", 811–816) |
| F-005 | The jitter draw happens inside `_schedule_next_run()`, so the interval changes on every reschedule and cannot be predicted from configuration; range validation is deferred to scheduling time (709–711) |
| F-006 | Deadlines are naive local datetimes and are therefore not timezone-corrected; five `strptime` formats are attempted in order (616–622); time-only strings are detected by the absence of `-` (626–631) |
| F-007 | `do()` is the only registration path and must remain the last statement after validation (657–663); `functools.partial` retains strong references to the callable and its arguments for the job's lifetime |
| F-008 | The decorator must return the undecorated function (911); it cannot be applied to non-static class methods (`docs/examples.rst`) |
| F-009 | Resolution is bounded by the caller's polling frequency; missed occurrences are never replayed (docstring 93–97); `run_all` sleeps synchronously between jobs (120) |
| F-010 | The sentinel must be recognized both as a class and as an instance (174); `cancel_job` must never raise for an unscheduled job (156–160) |
| F-011 | Tags must be hashable (466–467); `clear()` mutates the list in place so the module-level `jobs` alias keeps pointing at the same object (145, 148) |
| F-012 | Both accessors must return `None` rather than raise when the registry is empty or the tag matches nothing (188–192, 204–205) |
| F-013 | Both methods must tolerate a `job_func` of `None` and callables without `__name__` (265–268, 290–300) |
| F-014 | Level is fixed at DEBUG and the library must not configure handlers or levels; messages must use lazy `%` formatting |
| F-015 | The eight shortcuts must stay one-line delegations so instance and module behavior cannot diverge (843–896); `jobs` is a live reference, and line 840 carries an inline `todo` questioning that choice |
| F-016 | The hierarchy `ScheduleError` → `ScheduleValueError` → `IntervalError` must be preserved so existing `except` clauses keep working; validation must precede registry mutation |
| F-017 | No required runtime dependency may be added; `py.typed` must remain in `package_data`; the suite must pass with **and** without `pytz`; annotations must satisfy `mypy -p schedule` on every supported interpreter |

### 2.4.3 Performance and Scalability Considerations

No performance target, SLA, or benchmark is published anywhere in this repository; the characteristics below are read from the algorithms themselves. The observable reference point is the full suite of 81 test methods completing in 0.12 s on Python 3.12.

| Feature | Performance characteristic | Scalability consideration |
|---|---|---|
| F-001 | O(1) `timedelta` arithmetic; the catch-up loop at 733–734 iterates once per elapsed period | A job left unpolled for a very long time costs one loop iteration per missed period on its next reschedule |
| F-002 | One `weekday()` comparison plus one `timedelta` addition | Constant regardless of job count |
| F-003 | One regex match at configuration time; one `replace()` per reschedule | Constant per job |
| F-004 | Up to two `normalize()` calls and two `utcoffset()` comparisons per reschedule (773–817) | The most expensive scheduling path; `pytz` zone objects are shared per job, and no zone database is loaded unless a timezone is requested |
| F-005 | One `random.randint` per reschedule | Jitter spreads load across processes running identical schedules |
| F-006 | Up to five `strptime` attempts at configuration; two comparisons per run | Expired jobs are removed automatically, so the registry does not grow unboundedly |
| F-007 | One `partial` construction plus one list append | Registration is O(1); memory grows linearly with job count because arguments are retained |
| F-008 | Executes once at definition time | No runtime cost |
| F-009 | Linear scan of the registry for `should_run`, then a sort of the due subset (99–101); `run_all` blocks for `delay_seconds` × job count | Throughput is bounded by the aggregate duration of jobs on the single calling thread; long jobs delay every other job, which is why `docs/index.rst` directs long work off the scheduler thread and `docs/parallel-execution.rst` supplies thread and queue patterns |
| F-010 | `list.remove` is linear in registry size | Self-cancelling jobs keep the registry small |
| F-011 | Tagging O(1) per tag; `get_jobs`/`clear` linear in registry size | Tag filtering is a scan, not an index — cost grows with job count |
| F-012 | One `min()` scan plus one subtraction | Called once per loop iteration in the `idle_seconds()` pattern, so cost is linear in job count per iteration |
| F-013 | String formatting only | Invoked per DEBUG record; negligible unless DEBUG logging is enabled |
| F-014 | Lazy formatting means no cost when no handler accepts DEBUG | Log volume scales with executions per unit time |
| F-015 | One extra function call per delegation | Multiple schedulers partition state but add no parallelism — each must be polled separately (`docs/multiple-schedulers.rst`) |
| F-016 | O(1) guards | Validation cost is paid once per configuration call, never per run |
| F-017 | Import cost limited to eight standard-library modules | A zero-dependency install keeps container images and audit surface minimal; twelve tox environments keep the matrix cost linear in supported versions |

### 2.4.4 Security Implications

The module contains no authentication, authorization, cryptography, network, subprocess, filesystem, deserialization, or dynamic-evaluation code (imports at `schedule/__init__.py` 41–48). The implications below are therefore about the trust boundaries the library creates for its host, not about protecting the library itself.

| Feature | Security implication |
|---|---|
| F-007 / F-009 | The caller-supplied callable is the trust boundary: it executes synchronously with the full privileges of the host process, and its exceptions are not caught (line 691), so an uncaught failure aborts the remaining due jobs for that call — `docs/exception-handling.rst` makes defensive wrapping the caller's responsibility |
| F-013 / F-014 | DEBUG records embed the job's rendered arguments via `str(job)`; enabling DEBUG on the `schedule` logger can therefore surface argument values, so secrets should not be bound as job arguments in such deployments |
| F-004 / F-017 | `pytz` is the only third-party runtime package and is optional and lazily imported, which keeps the default supply-chain surface at zero; timezone correctness depends on the installed `pytz` release |
| F-005 | `random` is used solely for load jitter and provides no unpredictability guarantee suitable for security purposes |
| F-015 | `default_scheduler` is process-global mutable state; unrelated components in the same process share one registry, and `schedule.jobs` exposes the live list rather than a copy (line 840) |
| F-011 / F-012 | `get_jobs()` returns a copy of the registry list, but the `Job` objects inside it are the live objects — callers can mutate scheduled jobs directly |
| F-006 / F-010 | Cancellation is cooperative and in-process only; there is no privileged or remote control path to stop a running job |
| F-003 / F-016 | All user-supplied configuration strings are validated against anchored regexes or a fixed `strptime` allow-list before use, and error messages echo only the offending configuration value |

### 2.5.4 Assumptions and Constraints

**Assumptions made in producing this section.**

| Assumption | Basis |
|---|---|
| Implemented behavior is the requirement | No requirements document, backlog, or acceptance-test specification exists in the repository, so §2.1 and §2.2 are reverse-derived from code, tests, and `docs/` |
| Every catalogued feature is complete | All 17 are present in release 1.2.2, carry passing tests, and the package is classified `Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable` in `setup.py` |
| Priorities reflect internal emphasis, not external mandate | Derived from call-graph centrality, share of the 81-method suite, and prominence in `README.rst` / `docs/index.rst`; no business priority statement exists in the tree |
| Documentation statements are authoritative contracts | `docs/` is built with `sphinx-build -W` in CI, so its published behavior claims are maintained deliberately |
| The test suite is the acceptance criteria of record | `test_schedule.py` runs in all 12 tox environments on every push and pull request against `master` |

**Constraints recorded from the repository.**

| Constraint | Source |
|---|---|
| Public datetimes are naive local values | `schedule/__init__.py` 740–747; `docs/timezones.rst` |
| Zero required runtime dependencies; `pytz` optional and lazily imported | `pyproject.toml`; `schedule/__init__.py` 499 |
| Python 3.7 minimum, 3.7–3.12 verified | `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
| Serial, in-line execution driven by the caller; no background thread | `schedule/__init__.py` 89–120; `docs/background-execution.rst`, `docs/parallel-execution.rst` |
| No persistence — schedule state is lost at process exit | Absence of any I/O in the module; `docs/index.rst` non-goals |
| Sub-second precision, concurrency, and workday/holiday calendars are out of scope | `docs/index.rst` non-goals |
| Job duration is not accounted for, and missed runs are never replayed | `docs/index.rst`; `run_pending` docstring 93–97 |
| Job exceptions are not caught by the library | `schedule/__init__.py` 691; `docs/exception-handling.rst` |
| Timezones are configurable only through `at()` | `schedule/__init__.py` 471–508; `docs/timezones.rst` |
| `@repeat` does not work on non-static class methods | `docs/examples.rst` |
| Formatting fixed to `black==20.8b1`; docs must build warning-free | `requirements-dev.txt`, `tox.ini`, `docs/development.rst` |
| Semantic versioning with a version string in both `setup.py` and `docs/conf.py` | `docs/development.rst` |

# 3. Technology Stack

## 3.1 Programming Languages

This repository is a **single-language runtime with a multi-language supporting cast**. Every line of executable product code is Python; the remaining languages present are declarative or markup formats that configure packaging, quality gates, continuous integration, and the documentation build. There is no compiled extension module, no second runtime, and no front-end application: `setup.py` declares no `ext_modules`, and a scan of all 32 tracked files found no JavaScript build tooling, `package.json`, or `node_modules`.

### 3.1.1 Language Inventory by Component

| Component | Language | Representative artifacts |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduler runtime (the shipped product) | Python | `schedule/__init__.py` (945 lines) |
| Type-information marker | PEP 561 marker file (0 bytes, no language) | `schedule/py.typed` |
| Test suite | Python (`unittest` + `unittest.mock`) | `test_schedule.py` (1,599 lines) |
| Distribution metadata (legacy path) | Python | `setup.py` (55 lines) |
| Distribution metadata (PEP 621 path) | TOML | `pyproject.toml` (26 lines) |
| Tool configuration | INI / CFG | `tox.ini` (38 lines), `setup.cfg` (2 lines) |
| Source-distribution rules | setuptools MANIFEST template | `MANIFEST.in` (8 lines) |
| Development dependency list | pip requirements format | `requirements-dev.txt` (11 entries) |
| Continuous integration | YAML (GitHub Actions schema) | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (91 lines) |
| Documentation content | reStructuredText | 13 pages under `docs/`, plus `README.rst`, `HISTORY.rst`, `AUTHORS.rst` |
| Documentation build configuration | Python | `docs/conf.py` (373 lines) |
| Documentation build driver | GNU Make | `docs/Makefile` (225 lines) |
| Documentation theme overrides | HTML (Jinja2 template) and CSS | `docs/_templates/sidebarintro.html`, `docs/_static/custom.css` |

### 3.1.2 Python: Version Range and Dialect Constraints

The supported interpreter range is declared in two places and enforced in a third, and all three agree:

| Declaration | Value | Location |
|---|---|---|
| PEP 621 requirement | `requires-python = ">= 3.7"` | `pyproject.toml` line 12 |
| setuptools requirement | `python_requires=">=3.7"` | `setup.py` line 54 |
| Trove classifiers | `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.7` through `3.12` | `setup.py` lines 46–51 |
| Verified matrix | `['3.7','3.8','3.9','3.10','3.11','3.12']` | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` line 17 |
| Tox environments | `py3{7,8,9,10,11,12}{,-pytz}` — 12 environments | `tox.ini` line 2 |
| Published support statement | "Schedule is tested on Python 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12" | `docs/installation.rst` lines 8–9 |

The 3.7 floor is not merely declared — the source code is written in a dialect that honours it. Static inspection of `schedule/__init__.py` confirms every one of the following:

| Dialect property | Observation | Why it matters at the 3.7 floor |
|---|---|---|
| Typing style | `from typing import Set, List, Optional, Callable, Union` (line 48); annotations such as `List["Job"]` (line 122) and `Set[Hashable]` (line 254) | Builtin generics (`list[int]`) require 3.9; the pre-PEP-585 `typing` forms keep 3.7/3.8 valid |
| Union syntax | Zero occurrences of PEP 604 `X \| Y` in annotations; `Union[str, int]` used instead (lines 529–530) | `X \| Y` annotations require 3.10 |
| Deferred annotations | No `from __future__ import annotations` anywhere | The module does not depend on postponed evaluation |
| Assignment expressions | Zero occurrences of `:=` | The walrus operator requires 3.8 |
| f-strings | None in the runtime module; formatting uses `.format()` twice and lazy `%` formatting in all six `logger.debug(...)` calls | Consistent with a conservative, long-lived formatting style and lazy log evaluation |
| Variable annotations | Used throughout `Job.__init__` (lines 227–255), e.g. `self.latest: Optional[int] = None` | PEP 526 is available from 3.6, so it is safe at the floor |
| Timezone provider | `zoneinfo` appears **nowhere** in the repository; `pytz` is imported lazily inside `Job.at()` (lines 498–508) | The stdlib `zoneinfo` module (PEP 615) exists only from 3.9, so a 3.7 floor rules it out without a conditional backport |
| Exported typing | `schedule/py.typed` (0 bytes) shipped via `package_data={"schedule": ["py.typed"]}` (`setup.py` line 20) | PEP 561 lets downstream type checkers consume the inline annotations |

The `zoneinfo` exclusion is the single most consequential language-version constraint in the system: it is the reason the optional timezone dependency is `pytz` rather than the standard library, and the reason `Job.at()` accepts only `str` or `pytz.BaseTzInfo` and raises `ScheduleValueError` for anything else.

### 3.1.3 Selection Criteria and Justification

Python is not a discretionary choice here — it is the product. The library's stated purpose in `schedule/__init__.py` and `README.rst` is to run *Python functions (or any other callable) periodically*, so the runtime language and the target language are necessarily identical. Within that constraint, the observable selection criteria are:

| Criterion | How the repository satisfies it |
|---|---|
| The product must schedule Python callables in-process | `Job.do()` binds any callable with `functools.partial`; there is no serialization boundary, so no cross-language interface is possible or needed |
| Zero-install friction for consumers | Pure Python with `dependencies = []` (`pyproject.toml` line 13) means `pip install schedule` needs no compiler, wheel matrix, or platform-specific artifact |
| Maximum reach across deployed interpreters | A 3.7 floor covers interpreters far older than the current release line, at the documented cost of forgoing newer syntax |
| Platform neutrality | `Operating System :: OS Independent` classifier (`setup.py` line 43); the runtime module touches no OS-specific API |
| Vendorability | `docs/installation.rst` lines 89–91 note the library "consists of a single sourcefile MIT licenced", so a consumer can copy one Python file if a package manager is unavailable |
| Static verifiability | Inline annotations plus `py.typed`, verified by `mypy -p schedule` in every tox environment (`tox.ini` line 24, `setup.cfg`) |

The supporting languages are each the conventional, lowest-friction choice for their job: TOML because PEP 621 mandates it for `[project]` metadata; YAML because GitHub Actions accepts nothing else; reStructuredText because Sphinx is the documentation engine (`docs/development.rst` line 38 links the docutils reST reference); INI because that is tox's and mypy's configuration format; and GNU Make only as the local convenience wrapper around `sphinx-build`.

Across the 32 tracked files (4,793 lines total), the distribution is dominated by Python, with reStructuredText documentation as the second-largest body of material — a ratio that reflects a library whose differentiator is human-friendly ergonomics and therefore documentation.

### 3.1.5 Language-Level Constraints and Dependencies

| Constraint | Evidence and consequence |
|---|---|
| Runtime imports are standard library only | `schedule/__init__.py` lines 41–48 import `collections.abc.Hashable`, `datetime`, `functools`, `logging`, `random`, `re`, `time`, and `typing` — nothing else at import time |
| No compiled code | `setup.py` declares no `ext_modules`; the package is pure Python, so no toolchain, ABI, or platform wheel matrix is involved |
| Test suite requires a POSIX interpreter | `test_schedule.py` lines 29–30 set `os.environ["TZ"]` and call `time.tzset()`, which exists only on Unix — this ties the *test* suite (not the library) to Unix runners, matching the `ubuntu-latest` CI runner |
| Interpreter floor blocks modern syntax | Because 3.7 must keep working, contributions cannot use the walrus operator, PEP 604 unions, builtin generics, or `zoneinfo` |
| Documentation language is fixed | `Natural Language :: English` classifier (`setup.py` line 52) and `language = "en"` in `docs/conf.py` line 78; all reStructuredText is English-only |
| Interpreter security currency | The declared range begins at Python 3.7, which reached upstream end-of-life on 27 June 2023; 3.8 (October 2024), 3.9 (October 2025) have also passed end-of-life, and 3.10 is scheduled for October 2026. As of the current date only 3.10 through 3.14 remain in upstream security support, so four of the six matrix interpreters are outside that window and the matrix contains no 3.13 or 3.14 entry. Because the library itself imports only the standard library, the exposure is inherited from the host interpreter rather than introduced by this package |
| Vestigial linter directive | `test_schedule.py` lines 9–11 carry `# pylint: disable-msg=R0201,C0111,E0102,R0904,R0901`, but pylint appears in neither `requirements-dev.txt` nor `tox.ini` — the comment is a historical artifact, not an active tool contract |


## 3.2 Frameworks &amp; Libraries

The defining framework decision in this system is a **negative** one: the shipped package uses no application framework at all. `README.rst` advertises the library as "Very lightweight and no external dependencies", and `pyproject.toml` line 13 makes that literal with `dependencies = []`. Consequently every framework named below is either (a) a standard-library module acting as the runtime substrate, or (b) a development-time framework that never reaches a consumer's environment.

### 3.2.1 Runtime Substrate: The Python Standard Library

The eight standard-library imports at `schedule/__init__.py` lines 41–48 collectively play the role a framework would otherwise play. There are no others, and none is optional.

| Standard library module | Role in the architecture | Primary anchor |
|---|---|---|
| `datetime` | The entire time model — `datetime`, `time`, and `timedelta` are the units of scheduling; `timedelta(**{unit: interval})` turns the fluent unit name directly into arithmetic | `_schedule_next_run` line 729 |
| `functools` | `functools.partial` binds the callable with its arguments; `functools.update_wrapper` copies its metadata so `__name__` survives for logging and `__repr__` | `Job.do` lines 644–664 |
| `logging` | The sole observability channel: one named logger, DEBUG level, lazy `%` formatting | `logger = logging.getLogger("schedule")` line 50 |
| `random` | `random.randint(interval, latest)` implements the inclusive jitter range behind `to()` | line 712 |
| `re` | Three anchored regular expressions validate `at()` clock strings per unit | lines 513, 518, 524 |
| `time` | `time.sleep(delay_seconds)` spaces forced executions in `run_all()` | line 120 |
| `collections.abc.Hashable` | Runtime type guard for job tags | `Job.tag` lines 457–469 |
| `typing` | `Set`, `List`, `Optional`, `Callable`, `Union` annotations across the public surface | line 48 and throughout |

Because `pytz` is imported *inside* `Job.at()` rather than at module scope, the import graph of a consumer that never uses timezones contains only these standard-library modules.

### 3.2.2 Development-Time Frameworks and Their Declared Versions

Two dependency files describe the development toolchain, and they do not fully overlap: `requirements-dev.txt` is the human-facing "install everything" list referenced by `docs/development.rst`, while `tox.ini` declares the minimal per-environment sets that CI actually executes.

| Framework / tool | Declared version | Declared in |

| `pytest` | unpinned | `requirements-dev.txt`, `tox.ini` `[testenv] deps` |
| `pytest-cov` | unpinned | `requirements-dev.txt`, `tox.ini` `[testenv] deps` |
| `pytest-flake8` | unpinned | `requirements-dev.txt` only |
| `mypy` | unpinned | `requirements-dev.txt`, `tox.ini` `[testenv] deps` |
| `types-pytz` | unpinned | `requirements-dev.txt`, `tox.ini` `[testenv] deps` |
| `pytz` | unpinned | `requirements-dev.txt`; `tox.ini` line 21 as the conditional factor `pytz: pytz` |
| `black` | **pinned `==20.8b1`** | `requirements-dev.txt` line 7 |
| `click` | **pinned `==8.0.4`** | `requirements-dev.txt` line 8 |
| `Sphinx` | unpinned | `requirements-dev.txt` |

### 3.2.3 Testing Framework Stack

The tests are written against the standard library's `unittest` and executed by `pytest` — a deliberate combination that keeps the test code runnable by any runner while gaining pytest's collection, verbosity, and plugin ecosystem.

| Layer | Choice | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Test authoring framework | `unittest` — `from unittest import mock, TestCase`; the single suite class is `SchedulerTests(TestCase)` | `test_schedule.py` lines 5, 96 |
| Test doubles | `unittest.mock.Mock`, wrapped by `make_mock_job(name=None)` which supplies `__name__` | `test_schedule.py` lines 33–36 |
| Determinism harness | POSIX `TZ` strings for Berlin, Auckland, Chatham, and UTC; `os.environ["TZ"] = TZ_BERLIN` plus `time.tzset()`; a `mock_datetime` context manager that substitutes a controlled `datetime` subclass | `test_schedule.py` lines 23–30, 39 |
| Runner and coverage | `py.test test_schedule.py schedule -v --cov schedule --cov-report term-missing` | `tox.ini` line 23 |
| Environment matrix | 12 tox environments so the suite runs with **and** without `pytz` on each interpreter | `tox.ini` line 2 |
| Optional-dependency guard | Timezone tests skip themselves when `pytz` is unavailable, which is what keeps the non-`pytz` environments green | `test_schedule.py` timezone helper and `setup_utc_offset_test` |

Note that the pytest invocation targets both `test_schedule.py` and the `schedule` package; the latter is included so coverage and doctest-bearing sources are collected. The suite is fast enough to be a routine local gate — 81 test methods complete in a fraction of a second on a current interpreter.

### 3.2.4 Static Typing and Formatting Frameworks

| Concern | Framework and invocation | Configuration |
|---|---|---|
| Static typing | `python -m mypy -p schedule --install-types --non-interactive` in every tox test environment | `setup.cfg` `[mypy] files=schedule`; stub package `types-pytz` in `[testenv] deps`; `--install-types` allows mypy to fetch missing stubs non-interactively |
| Type export to consumers | 0-byte `schedule/py.typed` shipped through `package_data` | `setup.py` line 20 |
| Code formatting | `black --check .` as a standalone tox environment and a standalone CI job | `tox.ini` lines 31–33; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 67–78 |
| Formatter version discipline | `black==20.8b1` with `click==8.0.4` | `requirements-dev.txt` lines 7–8; `docs/development.rst` line 33 |
| Typing escape hatch | A single `# type: ignore` at the `pytz.timezone(tz)` assignment, required because the attribute is assigned a `pytz` object while the parameter is annotated `Optional[str]` | `schedule/__init__.py` line 502 |

The black pin is worth calling out explicitly as a maintenance liability: `20.8b1` is a 2020 *pre-release* build, whereas black has since moved to calendar versioning with an annual stable-style policy (the current stable line is in the 26.x series). Any contributor who installs an unpinned black will produce diffs that fail `black --check .`, which is precisely why the pin and the instruction in `docs/development.rst` exist.

`docs/development.rst` line 39 states the choice plainly: the documentation "is processed using Sphinx using the alabaster theme".

| Element | Configuration | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Engine | Sphinx, `source_suffix = ".rst"`, `master_doc = "index"` | `docs/conf.py` lines 50, 57 |
| Extensions | `sphinx.ext.autodoc`, `sphinx.ext.todo`, `sphinx.ext.coverage`, `sphinx.ext.viewcode` | `docs/conf.py` lines 35–41 |
| Autodoc source resolution | `sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(".."))` so the local package is importable | `docs/conf.py` line 24 |
| Member ordering | `autodoc_member_order = "bysource"` | `docs/conf.py` line 370 |
| Theme | `html_theme = "alabaster"` with GitHub banner and star button for `dbader/schedule` | `docs/conf.py` lines 131–145 |
| Theme overrides | `_templates/sidebarintro.html` in the five-entry `html_sidebars["**"]` list; `_static/custom.css` | `docs/conf.py` lines 173, 194–202 |
| Version stamp | `version = "1.2.2"` and `release = "1.2.2"` — a second hard-coded copy of the release number | `docs/conf.py` lines 69–71 |
| reST toolchain | `docutils` (parser) and `Pygments` (code highlighting) as dev requirements | `requirements-dev.txt` lines 1–2 |
| Local build | `cd docs && make html`, output in `docs/_build/html` | `docs/Makefile`, `docs/development.rst` lines 44–47 |

Because `sphinx-build` runs with `-W`, the docstrings inside `schedule/__init__.py` are effectively part of the build contract: a malformed `:meth:` reference fails CI. `suppress_warnings = ["image.nonlocal_uri"]` (`docs/conf.py` line 373) is the one deliberate exemption, needed because `README.rst` embeds remote badge images.

### 3.2.6 Compatibility Requirements

| Requirement | Enforcement point |
|---|---|
| The package must import and pass its suite on Python 3.7 through 3.12 | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` matrix × `tox.ini` `[gh-actions]` mapping |
| The package must behave identically with and without `pytz` installed | `tox.ini` factor-conditional dependency `pytz: pytz` producing 12 environments |
| `pytz` must satisfy `Job.at()`'s type contract (`str` or `pytz.BaseTzInfo`) | `schedule/__init__.py` lines 501–508; `test_tz_invalid_timezone_exceptions` |
| mypy must resolve `pytz` symbols | `types-pytz` stub package in `[testenv] deps` and `requirements-dev.txt` |
| `black==20.8b1` requires `click==8.0.4` | Paired pins in `requirements-dev.txt`; verified by the `formatting` CI job |
| The build backend must support PEP 621 `[project]` metadata with `dynamic` fields | `requires = ["setuptools >= 61.0"]` in `pyproject.toml` |
| `setup.py` and `pyproject.toml` must not disagree | `dynamic = ["version","classifiers","keywords","authors"]` delegates exactly those four fields to `setup.py`; the `setuppy` CI job runs `setup.py check --strict --metadata --restructuredtext` |
| `docs/conf.py` and `setup.py` version strings must match | Manual step mandated by `docs/development.rst` line 53; no automated assertion exists |
| The documentation must build without warnings on Python 3.11 | `docs` CI job running `tox -e docs` |
| `README.rst` must be valid reStructuredText for PyPI rendering | `setup.py check --restructuredtext` in the `setuppy` CI job |

### 3.2.7 Justification for the Major Framework Choices

| Choice | Justification grounded in the repository |
|---|---|
| No runtime framework; standard library only | The product promise is "no external dependencies" (`README.rst`); an in-process scheduler embedded in arbitrary host applications must not impose transitive dependencies or version conflicts on its host |
| `unittest` for authoring, `pytest` for running | `unittest` keeps the suite dependency-free and executable by any runner (relevant because `MANIFEST.in` ships `test_schedule.py` inside the sdist); `pytest` supplies the coverage plugin and readable output used by the gate command |
| `tox` as the matrix orchestrator | It is the only mechanism in the repository capable of expressing "each interpreter, with and without the optional extra" as a single declarative envlist, and `tox-gh-actions` maps that envlist onto the CI matrix without duplicating it |
| `mypy` plus `py.typed` | The library is a typed API surface consumed by other codebases; exporting annotations is only credible if they are machine-checked, so the type gate runs alongside the tests in every environment |
| `black` with a hard pin | Formatting is enforced as a blocking CI job, so the formatter version must be deterministic or the gate becomes flaky across contributors |
| Sphinx with `-W` | Documentation is the product's differentiator; treating warnings as errors prevents silent decay of the 13 published pages and the autodoc reference |
| `setuptools` (not a modern alternative backend) | The project predates PEP 621 by a decade; keeping `setuptools` allows the incremental migration visible today, where static metadata lives in `pyproject.toml` while version/classifiers/keywords/authors remain in `setup.py` |
| `pytz` rather than `zoneinfo` | Forced by the Python 3.7 floor, since `zoneinfo` is only available from 3.9 onward |


## 3.3 Open Source Dependencies

The dependency budget of this project is unusually easy to state: **zero required runtime dependencies, one optional runtime dependency, and eleven declared development dependencies.** `pyproject.toml` line 13 reads `dependencies = []`, and `docs/installation.rst` line 17 states "Schedule has 1 optional dependency".

### 3.3.1 Runtime Dependencies

| Tier | Package | Declared version | Declaration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Required | *(none)* | — | `pyproject.toml` line 13: `dependencies = []` |
| Optional extra `timezone` | `pytz` | unpinned — no floor and no ceiling | `pyproject.toml` lines 19–20 |

`pytz` is the only third-party package that can ever be present at runtime, and it is reachable only through one code path: `Job.at(time_str, tz)` executes `import pytz` inside the method body when — and only when — a `tz` argument is supplied (`schedule/__init__.py` lines 498–508). A consumer that never passes a timezone never imports it, which is what makes an empty required-dependency list truthful rather than aspirational.

Two documentation-versus-packaging observations are worth recording because they affect how consumers actually install the extra:

- The declared extra is `timezone`, but the extras-install form `schedule[timezone]` appears **nowhere** in the repository. `docs/timezones.rst` line 13 and `docs/faq.rst` line 50 instead instruct users to run `pip install pytz` directly, and `docs/faq.rst` lines 45–50 document the resulting `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytz'` as an expected failure mode with that resolution.
- Because `pytz` carries no version constraint, timezone correctness depends on whichever `pytz` release — and therefore whichever IANA tz database snapshot — the consumer happens to have installed.

### 3.3.5 Supply-Chain and Security Implications

| Implication | Basis in the repository |
|---|---|
| Default attack surface is a single file | Zero required dependencies means no transitive packages to audit, pin, or patch; the shipped artifact is `schedule/__init__.py` plus a 0-byte marker |
| The optional dependency is also the only third-party trust decision | `pytz` is unpinned in `pyproject.toml`, so consumers inherit whatever release their resolver selects; `types-pytz` matters only at development time |
| No dependency lock file exists | Neither a lock file nor hash pinning is present; `requirements-dev.txt` pins only `black` and `click`, so a development or CI environment is reproducible only to the resolution date |
| CI installs unpinned tooling from PyPI on every run | `pip install tox tox-gh-actions` and `pip3 install coveralls` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` fetch latest releases at execution time, and `mypy --install-types` may fetch additional stub packages mid-run |
| Actions are pinned by mutable major tags | `actions/checkout@v3` and `actions/setup-python@v4` resolve to a moving target rather than a commit SHA |
| The library performs no deserialization, network, or subprocess work | Verified absence of `open()`, `pickle`, `json`, `socket`, `subprocess`, `os`/`environ` access, `eval`, and `exec` anywhere in `schedule/__init__.py`, so there is no untrusted-input parsing path other than the caller's own configuration strings |
| Randomness is not cryptographic | `random.randint` (line 712) implements schedule jitter only and offers no unpredictability guarantee |
| A stale formatter pin is a known-quantity risk | `black==20.8b1` is a 2020 pre-release; black's current stable line is calendar-versioned in the 26.x series, so the pinned build no longer receives fixes. It is a development-only dependency and therefore never reaches consumers |
| End-of-life interpreters are inside the declared support range | Python 3.7, 3.8 and 3.9 are past upstream end-of-life (June 2023, October 2024 and October 2025 respectively) and 3.10 is scheduled for October 2026, yet all four remain in the CI matrix; the package inherits, rather than causes, that exposure since it imports only the standard library |


## 3.4 Third-Party Services

The shipped library integrates with **no external service whatsoever**. Every third-party service identified below sits on the *engineering* side of the boundary — source hosting, continuous integration, coverage reporting, package distribution, and documentation publishing — and none of them is reachable from, or required by, the runtime.

### 3.4.1 Runtime External Integrations: Verified Absent

| Service category | Status in this system | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| External / third-party APIs | None | No HTTP client, socket, or RPC construct exists in `schedule/__init__.py`; a keyword scan across all 32 tracked files found no `requests`, `httpx`, `urllib3`, or `aiohttp` usage |
| Authentication / identity providers | None | No authentication or authorization concept exists anywhere in the package; no `jwt`, `oauth`, `auth0`, `passlib`, `bcrypt`, or `cryptography` reference exists in any tracked file |
| Cloud platform services | None | No `boto3`/`botocore`, AWS CLI, Azure, or Google Cloud SDK reference; no cloud credential handling |
| Message brokers / queues | None ship with the package | `docs/parallel-execution.rst` shows a caller-side `queue.Queue` worker pattern and mentions beanstalkd only as an illustration; no broker client is imported |
| APM / metrics / tracing backends | None | No Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Sentry, Datadog, New Relic, or statsd reference; the only telemetry is `logging` at DEBUG on the `schedule` logger (`schedule/__init__.py` line 50) |
| Secret / configuration management | None | The library reads no environment variable and no configuration file; jobs are configured exclusively through Python API calls |
| Time / NTP services | None | Time comes from `datetime.datetime.now()` and, when requested, a `pytz` zone object |

### 3.4.3 Authentication and Credential Handling

There is no authentication *feature* in this system and no identity provider integration. The only credentials that appear anywhere in the repository are CI and publishing credentials, and both are held outside the tree:

| Credential | Scope and handling | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Injected as `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` into the Coveralls steps of the `test` and `coverage push` jobs; the automatically provisioned per-run token, never a long-lived secret | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 30, 52 |
| PyPI / TestPyPI upload credentials | Referenced only indirectly through the twine repository aliases `schedule` and `schedule-test`; the aliases resolve to a maintainer's local `.pypirc`, which is not present in the repository | `docs/development.rst` lines 63–66 |

No other secret, token, key, or credential reference exists in any tracked file, and no `.env` file or secret-management integration is present.

### 3.4.4 Monitoring and Observability Services

| Layer | What exists | What does not |
|---|---|---|
| Library runtime | A single `logging.getLogger("schedule")` emitting DEBUG records for run, run-all, cancel, and clear operations, documented in `docs/logging.rst`; the library installs no handler and sets no level | No metrics exporter, no tracing, no health endpoint, no error-reporting SDK |
| Engineering telemetry | Coveralls receives per-interpreter coverage with `COVERALLS_FLAG_NAME=python-<version>` and `COVERALLS_PARALLEL=true`, then a dependent job calls `coveralls --finish` so the service can combine results and post a summary; three README badges surface CI status, coverage, and the published PyPI version | No uptime monitoring, dashboarding, or alerting service — there is no deployed system to monitor |

The design consequence is that all runtime observability is delegated to the host application: because the library only emits standard `logging` records, whatever monitoring stack the host already uses receives scheduler diagnostics with no additional integration.

### 3.4.5 Cloud Services

No cloud service is used, referenced, or provisioned by this repository. There is no infrastructure-as-code, no deployment target, and no cloud account dependency; the only remote compute involved is the GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner pool that executes `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and the only remote storage involved is the package and documentation hosting listed in 3.4.2. This is a direct consequence of the product form factor established in the earlier sections of this specification: the artifact is a library that runs inside someone else's process, so it has no infrastructure of its own to describe.


## 3.5 Databases &amp; Storage

This system has **no database tier, no cache tier, and no storage service**. That is not an omission in the documentation — it is a published product boundary. `docs/index.rst` lists job persistence first among the reasons to choose a different library, stating that Schedule will not remember the schedule between restarts.

### 3.5.1 Primary and Secondary Databases

| Category | Status | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| Primary database | None | A keyword scan of all 32 tracked files found no reference to MongoDB/`pymongo`, SQLAlchemy, `psycopg`, MySQL, `sqlite3`, or any other driver or ORM |
| Secondary / analytical store | None | Same scan; no data-warehouse or reporting integration exists |
| Migration tooling | None | No migration directory, schema file, or DDL of any kind is present |
| Connection configuration | None | `schedule/__init__.py` reads no environment variable and parses no configuration file |

### 3.5.2 The Only State Store: An In-Memory Job Registry

All state in the system lives in one Python list for the lifetime of the host process.

| Element | Definition | Location |
|---|---|---|
| The registry | `self.jobs: List[Job] = []` on each `Scheduler` instance | `schedule/__init__.py` line 87 |
| The process-global instance | `default_scheduler = Scheduler()` | line 837 |
| The public alias | `jobs = default_scheduler.jobs` — a live reference, not a copy, carrying an inline `todo` questioning that choice | line 840 |
| Record shape | Each `Job` holds `interval`, `latest`, `unit`, `at_time`, `at_time_zone`, `start_day`, `cancel_after`, `tags`, `last_run`, `next_run`, a back-reference to its `scheduler`, and `job_func` (a `functools.partial` retaining the callable and its bound arguments) | `Job.__init__` lines 227–255 |
| Write path | `Job.do()` appends the job only after validation and first-next-run computation succeed | lines 657–663 |
| Read paths | `get_jobs(tag)` returns a *copy of the list* (the `Job` objects inside remain live); `get_next_run(tag)` returns `min(...).next_run`; `idle_seconds` derives from it | lines 122–133, 177–206 |
| Delete paths | `clear(tag)` mutates the list **in place** (`del self.jobs[:]` or slice assignment) so the module-level alias stays valid; `cancel_job()` removes one entry and silently ignores an unscheduled job | lines 135–160 |
| Isolation model | Independent `Scheduler()` instances own independent registries, each requiring its own `run_pending()` call | `docs/multiple-schedulers.rst` |

### 3.5.3 Data Persistence Strategy

The persistence strategy is *deliberately none*: state is created by API calls, mutated by scheduling arithmetic, and discarded when the process exits.

| Aspect | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Durability | Zero. There is no serialization anywhere in the module — no `pickle`, `json`, `shelve`, `dbm`, or `open()` call exists in `schedule/__init__.py` |
| Recovery model | The host application must re-register its jobs on every startup; the canonical usage pattern in `README.rst` does exactly that, in code, before entering the `run_pending()` loop |
| Retention | Bounded by process lifetime; expired `until()` jobs and self-cancelling `CancelJob` jobs are removed from the registry automatically, so it does not grow without bound |
| Consistency model | Single-threaded, in-line mutation with no locking; there is no transaction, no concurrent writer, and therefore no isolation level to describe |
| Cross-process sharing | None. `default_scheduler` is process-global mutable state shared by every component in the same interpreter, and nothing is shared across processes |

### 3.5.4 Caching Solutions

No caching layer exists, and no memoization decorator is used anywhere in the runtime module (`functools.lru_cache` is absent). Two retention behaviours are sometimes mistaken for caching and are worth distinguishing:

- **Bound-argument retention.** `job_func = functools.partial(job_func, *args, **kwargs)` keeps strong references to the callable and its arguments for the job's entire lifetime (`Job.do`, lines 644–664). This is binding, not caching, and it is why registry memory grows linearly with job count.
- **Timezone-object retention.** When `at(time_str, tz)` is given a zone, the resolved `pytz` object is stored on the job as `at_time_zone` (lines 500–503) and reused on every reschedule. This avoids repeated zone lookups per job but is not a shared cache — each job holds its own reference, and no zone data is loaded at all unless a timezone is requested.

### 3.5.5 Storage Services

There is no object store, block store, file store, or blob service. The only filesystem activity anywhere in the repository is development-time and build-time:

| Filesystem interaction | Purpose | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `codecs.open(filename, "r", "utf8")` reading `README.rst` | Supplies `long_description` for packaging metadata | `setup.py` lines 9–14, 23 |
| `sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(".."))` | Makes the package importable for Sphinx autodoc | `docs/conf.py` line 24 |
| `sphinx-build` output into `_build` / `{envtmpdir}` | Documentation artifacts, git-ignored | `docs/Makefile`, `tox.ini` line 29, `.gitignore` line 44 |
| Coverage and tox working directories | `.coverage`, `.tox`, `dist`, `build`, `*.egg-info` | `.gitignore` lines 7–27 |

### 3.5.6 Implications for Consumers

Because there is no storage tier, durability is entirely the host application's responsibility. Any consumer requiring restart-surviving schedules must re-declare jobs at startup or adopt a different scheduler; any consumer requiring shared schedule state across processes must coordinate that externally, since each `Scheduler` is process-local with no leader election, locking, or shared registry. This division of responsibility is stated as a non-goal in `docs/index.rst` rather than left for consumers to discover, and it is the reason the package needs no configuration, no connection string, and no credentials.


## 3.6 Development &amp; Deployment

"Deployment" for this system means **publishing a package**, not operating a service. There is no runtime environment to provision, so the toolchain is organised around a matrix of interpreter environments, five blocking quality gates, and a manual, documented publication ritual.

### 3.6.1 Development Environment and Tools

| Concern | Tooling and command | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Dependency bootstrap | `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` | `docs/development.rst` lines 8–12 |
| Test execution (documented) | `py.test test_schedule.py --flake8 schedule -v --cov schedule --cov-report term-missing` | `docs/development.rst` line 22 |
| Test execution (enforced) | `py.test test_schedule.py schedule -v --cov schedule --cov-report term-missing` — note the absence of `--flake8` | `tox.ini` line 23 |
| Formatting | `black .` locally; "Make sure you use version 20.8b1 of black" | `docs/development.rst` lines 26–33 |
| Type checking | `python -m mypy -p schedule --install-types --non-interactive` | `tox.ini` line 24, `setup.cfg` |
| Documentation preview | `cd docs && make html`, output in `docs/_build/html` | `docs/development.rst` lines 44–47, `docs/Makefile` |
| Multi-interpreter runs | `tox` (12 environments) | `tox.ini` |
| Editor / IDE assumptions | `.gitignore` excludes JetBrains artifacts (`.idea`, `*.iml`) and virtualenv directories (`env`, `env3`, `venv`), so local environments are developer-chosen rather than prescribed | `.gitignore` lines 38–48 |
| Version control conventions | Single `master` branch is the CI target for both pushes and pull requests; releases are annotated tags `X.Y.Z` | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 3–9; `docs/development.rst` line 58 |

There is no devcontainer, no editor configuration file, no pre-commit configuration, and no `Makefile` at the repository root — the only `Makefile` is the Sphinx build driver under `docs/`.

### 3.6.2 Build System

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Build backend | `setuptools.build_meta` | `pyproject.toml` line 3 |
| Build requirement | `setuptools >= 61.0` (the floor that provides PEP 621 `[project]` support) | `pyproject.toml` line 2 |
| Static metadata | `name`, `description`, `readme`, `license`, `requires-python`, `dependencies`, `maintainers`, optional-dependencies, and four project URLs | `pyproject.toml` |
| Dynamic metadata | `version`, `classifiers`, `keywords`, `authors` — deliberately delegated to `setup.py` | `pyproject.toml` line 8 |
| Version source of truth | `SCHEDULE_VERSION = "1.2.2"` | `setup.py` line 5 (duplicated as `version`/`release` in `docs/conf.py` lines 69–71) |
| Package contents | `packages=["schedule"]` plus `package_data={"schedule": ["py.typed"]}` | `setup.py` lines 19–20 |
| Source-distribution contents | `README.rst`, `HISTORY.rst`, `LICENSE.txt`, `test_schedule.py`; `__pycache__` and `*.py[co]` excluded recursively — note that `docs/` is not shipped | `MANIFEST.in` |
| Wheel construction | `python3 -m build --wheel` after `pip install --upgrade setuptools twine wheel` | `docs/development.rst` lines 61–62 |
| Compilation steps | None — the distribution is pure Python with no `ext_modules` | `setup.py` |

The hybrid metadata arrangement is the notable characteristic here: this is a decade-old setuptools project mid-migration to PEP 621, and the `dynamic` declaration is what keeps the two files from conflicting. The `setuppy` CI gate exists precisely to catch a divergence, since `python setup.py check --strict --metadata --restructuredtext` validates both the metadata completeness and the reStructuredText that PyPI will render.

### 3.6.3 Quality Gates

Five distinct gates are declared in `tox.ini` and each is wired into CI. All are blocking.

| Gate | tox environment | Command and failure condition |
|---|---|---|
| Tests + coverage | `py3{7..12}{,-pytz}` (12 envs) | `py.test test_schedule.py schedule -v --cov schedule --cov-report term-missing` — any failing test fails the build; `skip_missing_interpreters = true` prevents a missing local interpreter from erroring |
| Static typing | same 12 envs | `python -m mypy -p schedule --install-types --non-interactive` — any type error fails the build |
| Documentation | `docs` | `sphinx-build -W -b html …` — **any warning** fails the build |
| Formatting | `format` | `black --check .` — any deviation from `black==20.8b1` output fails the build |
| Packaging metadata | `setuppy` | `python setup.py check --strict --metadata --restructuredtext` — incomplete metadata or invalid reST fails the build |

The optional-dependency contract is enforced structurally rather than by assertion: `tox.ini` line 21 declares `pytz` as the factor-conditional dependency `pytz: pytz`, so each interpreter is exercised once *with* and once *without* `pytz`, and the timezone tests skip themselves when it is absent.

### 3.6.4 Continuous Integration Topology

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` defines a workflow named `Tests` triggered on pushes to `master` and pull requests targeting `master`. It contains five jobs, all on `ubuntu-latest`; Python 3.11 is the fixed utility interpreter for the four non-matrix jobs.

| Job | Trigger relationship | Work performed |
|---|---|---|
| `test` | Runs on every event; `max-parallel: 6` across `['3.7','3.8','3.9','3.10','3.11','3.12']` | `actions/checkout@v3`, `actions/setup-python@v4`, `pip install tox tox-gh-actions`, `tox`, then a Coveralls upload flagged `python-<version>` with `COVERALLS_PARALLEL=true` |
| `coveralls` (display name `coverage push`) | `needs: test` | `coveralls --finish --service=github` so the service combines the parallel results and posts the summary comment; this job performs no checkout |
| `docs` | Independent | `tox -e docs` |
| `formatting` | Independent | `tox -e format` |
| `setuppy` | Independent | `tox -e setuppy` (its step is labelled "Check docs", a cosmetic mislabel) |

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Trigger["Event: push or pull_request<br/>branch master"]
    subgraph TestJob["test job — ubuntu-latest, max-parallel 6"]
        Checkout["actions/checkout@v3<br/>actions/setup-python@v4"]
        MatrixNode["Matrix: 3.7 / 3.8 / 3.9 / 3.10 / 3.11 / 3.12"]
        ToxRun["pip install tox tox-gh-actions<br/>then run tox"]
        EnvPair["Per version via tox-gh-actions:<br/>pyXX and pyXX-pytz"]
        Gate1["pytest + coverage, then mypy -p schedule"]
        CovUp["coveralls --service=github<br/>flag python-X.Y, parallel"]
    end
    subgraph FanInJob["coverage push job — needs test"]
        Finish["coveralls --finish --service=github"]
    end
    subgraph GateJobs["Independent gate jobs — Python 3.11"]
        DocsGate["docs: tox -e docs<br/>sphinx-build -W"]
        FormatGate["formatting: tox -e format<br/>black --check ."]
        MetaGate["setuppy: tox -e setuppy<br/>setup.py check --strict"]
    end
    Trigger --> Checkout
    Checkout --> MatrixNode
    MatrixNode --> ToxRun
    ToxRun --> EnvPair
    EnvPair --> Gate1
    Gate1 --> CovUp
    CovUp --> Finish
    Trigger --> DocsGate
    Trigger --> FormatGate
    Trigger --> MetaGate
```

The `[gh-actions]` table in `tox.ini` is the hinge between the two configuration files: GitHub Actions supplies one interpreter per matrix entry, and `tox-gh-actions` expands that single interpreter into the pair of environments (`pyXX`, `pyXX-pytz`) declared in the envlist — so twelve environments are covered by six matrix entries without duplicating the matrix in YAML.

`HISTORY.rst` records that this platform choice was itself a migration: release 1.0.0 "Replaced Travis with Github Actions for automated testing". No Travis configuration remains in the tree.

### 3.6.5 Release and Publication Pipeline

Publication is **not automated** — there is no release, tag, or publish workflow in `.github/workflows/`. The process is a documented manual sequence in `docs/development.rst` lines 49–68, executed by a maintainer:

```bash
git tag X.Y.Z -m "Release X.Y.Z" && git push --tags
python3 -m build --wheel && twine upload --repository schedule-test dist/*
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Step1["Update HISTORY.rst<br/>and AUTHORS.rst"]
    Step2["Bump version in setup.py<br/>AND docs/conf.py"]
    Step3["Merge to master<br/>CI gates must pass"]
    Step4["git tag X.Y.Z<br/>git push --tags"]
    Step5["python3 -m build --wheel"]
    Step6["twine upload<br/>repository schedule-test<br/>(TestPyPI)"]
    Step7["twine upload<br/>repository schedule<br/>(PyPI)"]
    Step8["Downstream channels<br/>Ubuntu / Debian / AUR / conda-forge"]
    Step1 --> Step2
    Step2 --> Step3
    Step3 --> Step4
    Step4 --> Step5
    Step5 --> Step6
    Step6 -->|verified| Step7
    Step7 --> Step8
```

Two properties of this pipeline are load-bearing. First, the version number exists in two files (`setup.py` line 5 and `docs/conf.py` lines 69–71) and nothing verifies that they agree, so the dual bump in step 2 is a manual invariant. Second, the project declares semantic versioning (`docs/development.rst` line 68), which is what makes the naive-local `next_run` contract documented elsewhere in this specification a breaking-change concern rather than an implementation detail.

### 3.6.6 Containerization and Infrastructure

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| Containerization | **Absent.** No `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, or compose file exists anywhere in the repository |
| Container registry | Not applicable — no image is built or published |
| Infrastructure as code | **Absent.** No Terraform (`*.tf`), CloudFormation, Helm chart, Kubernetes manifest, or Ansible playbook exists |
| Orchestration / runtime platform | Not applicable — the artifact is a library that executes inside a consumer's process |
| Environment configuration | None — no `.env` file, no environment-variable contract, and no configuration file format |
| Alternative CI platforms | None — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the only automation file; no Travis, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, or Azure Pipelines configuration is present |

This is the single largest divergence from the default technology stack proposed for greenfield projects (AWS, Docker, Terraform): none of those layers is applicable to a zero-dependency pure-Python library, and introducing them would contradict the "no extra processes needed" positioning stated in `README.rst`. The only element of that default stack actually present is GitHub Actions, plus Python itself.

### 3.6.7 CI/CD Requirements and Observed Gaps

Requirements that any change to this repository must satisfy, all mechanically enforced:

1. Green tests **and** a clean mypy run on all six interpreters, both with and without `pytz` (12 environments).
2. A warning-free Sphinx build, which transitively requires well-formed docstrings in `schedule/__init__.py` because `sphinx.ext.autodoc` consumes them.
3. Byte-identical formatting under `black==20.8b1`.
4. Valid, complete packaging metadata and PyPI-renderable reStructuredText.
5. Coverage published to Coveralls per interpreter and aggregated by the dependent job.

Gaps observable in the configuration, recorded as facts rather than recommendations:

| Gap | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Linting is documented but not enforced | `pytest-flake8` is a declared dev dependency and `docs/development.rst` line 22 passes `--flake8`, but the CI-enforced command in `tox.ini` line 23 omits it |
| No dependency pinning or lock file | Only `black` and `click` are pinned; `tox`, `tox-gh-actions`, and `coveralls` are installed unpinned at CI runtime |
| Actions referenced by mutable major tags | `actions/checkout@v3` and `actions/setup-python@v4` rather than commit SHAs |
| Publication is manual | No release/publish workflow exists; tagging, building, and both twine uploads are performed by hand |
| Documentation hosting is configured out-of-tree | `schedule.readthedocs.io` is the declared documentation URL, but no `.readthedocs.yaml` exists in the repository |
| Single-platform verification | Every job runs on `ubuntu-latest` despite the `Operating System :: OS Independent` classifier; the test suite's use of `time.tzset()` would in any case require adaptation for a Windows runner |
| No coverage threshold | Coverage is measured and reported (`--cov-report term-missing`) and uploaded, but no minimum is enforced in `tox.ini` or the workflow |
| Version duplication is unverified | `setup.py` and `docs/conf.py` both hard-code `1.2.2` with no automated consistency check |
