## 9.4 Supplementary Environment and Housekeeping Reference

This appendix collects the remaining verified detail that earlier sections cite only by count: the literal timezone data the test suite depends on, the repository's exclusion rules, the attribution and licensing artifacts, the in-source annotation census, and the external context behind the one load-bearing tool pin.

### 9.4.1 Test Determinism Reference Data

Section 6.6.6.2 records that the suite pins the process timezone with a POSIX `TZ` string and calls `time.tzset()`. The four constants themselves are reproduced here because they are opaque C-library expressions whose meaning is not recoverable from the constant names alone, and because they — not IANA names — are what make the assertions deterministic.

| Constant | POSIX `TZ` value | Rules encoded |
|---|---|---|
| `TZ_BERLIN` | `CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3` | UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 summer; last Sunday of March to last Sunday of October at 03:00 |
| `TZ_AUCKLAND` | `NZST-12NZDT,M9.5.0,M4.1.0/3` | UTC+12 standard, UTC+13 summer; southern-hemisphere transition order |
| `TZ_CHATHAM` | `<+1245>-12:45<+1345>,M9.5.0/2:45,M4.1.0/3:45` | Quarter-hour offsets (UTC+12:45 / +13:45) with quarter-hour transition times |
| `TZ_UTC` | `UTC0` | Fixed zero offset, no DST |

`TZ_BERLIN` is applied at module import, so it governs every test that does not override it; the other three are supplied per block through the `zone` argument of `mock_datetime`. `TZ_CHATHAM` is the reason the suite can assert non-integral-hour offsets at all, and it is applied as a POSIX rule rather than as `Pacific/Chatham` because it must take effect at the process level rather than inside the library.

Exactly fifteen distinct IANA zone names are passed to the library across the suite — the figure Section 1.2.3.3 reports as a count. Enumerated with their occurrence counts: `Europe/Berlin` (8), `Europe/London` (3), `Europe/Amsterdam` (2), `Canada/Newfoundland` (2), `Australia/Sydney` (2), `Asia/Kathmandu` (2), `America/New_York` (2), and one occurrence each of `US/Eastern`, `US/Central`, `Europe/Istanbul`, `Asia/Tokyo`, `Asia/Krasnoyarsk`, `Asia/Kolkata`, `Asia/Dubai`, and `America/Anchorage`. The distribution is deliberate: Berlin dominates because it is also the pinned process zone, Kathmandu and Chatham supply non-integral offsets, Newfoundland pairs a half-hour offset with a DST rule, and Sydney with Auckland provide southern-hemisphere transition directions that oppose the northern ones.

### 9.4.3 Attribution and Licensing Artifacts

| Artifact | Structure | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTHORS.rst` | One introductory sentence plus a flat bulleted roll of contributor handles, each with a GitHub profile link | Cumulative credit; included into the published site by `docs/index.rst` |
| `HISTORY.rst` | Per-change "Thanks @handle!" annotations inline with each release entry | Contribution-level attribution tied to the change it credits |
| `LICENSE.txt` | The unmodified MIT text, "Copyright (c) 2013 Daniel Bader (http://dbader.org)" | The licence grant shipped with every artifact |

The roll in `AUTHORS.rst` contains 45 bulleted entries as measured directly against the file (one of which carries a second, Bitbucket profile link in addition to the GitHub one); this is one fewer than the contributor figure cited in Section 1.2.3.2, and the discrepancy is recorded here so that the measured value and its measurement basis — bullet lines only, excluding the introductory sentence — are unambiguous. Entries are appended in contribution order rather than sorted, which makes the file itself a rough chronology. The two-file model means credit is recorded twice by design: `AUTHORS.rst` answers "who has contributed", `HISTORY.rst` answers "who contributed what".

The MIT grant decomposes as follows, quoted in substance from `LICENSE.txt`: permission is granted without restriction to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense and sell the software; the single condition is that the copyright notice and the permission notice accompany all copies or substantial portions; and all warranties — expressly including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement — are disclaimed, with no liability accepted for any claim or damages. Section 8.1.1.5 records how the file is mechanically attached to each artifact. The practical consequence for the manual-vendoring path published in `docs/installation.rst` is that a consumer who copies `schedule/__init__.py` into their own tree inherits the notice-retention condition even though the copied file contains no licence header of its own.

### 9.4.4 In-Source Annotation Census

A repository-wide scan of the Python, reST, INI, TOML, CFG and YAML files yields a short and complete list of engineering annotations, recorded here because the absence of accumulated `FIXME`/`XXX`/`HACK` debt markers in a decade-old codebase is itself a finding.

| Annotation | Occurrences | Location and purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `# type: ignore` | 3 | Reading `__name__` off a bound callable; `pytz.timezone(tz)` assignment; `moment.replace(**kwargs)` — all in `schedule/__init__.py` |
| `# todo` | 1 | On the module-level `jobs` alias, asking whether it should be a copy or a function |
| `pylint: disable-msg` | 1 block | `test_schedule.py` silencing R0201, C0111, E0102, R0904, R0901 |
| `FIXME`, `XXX`, `HACK`, deprecation markers | 0 | None anywhere in the tree |

The three `type: ignore` comments are the exact points at which the annotated implementation exceeds what `mypy` can verify, so they delimit the boundary of the type contract that Section 6.6.3.2 describes as the project's closest analogue to contract testing. The `todo` annotation is the only open design question recorded in code, and it is consequential: `jobs = default_scheduler.jobs` binds the module-level name to the *same list object* the default scheduler mutates, and `Scheduler.clear()` empties it in place (`del self.jobs[:]`) rather than rebinding, so the alias remains valid across clears. By contrast `get_jobs()` returns `self.jobs[:]`, a snapshot copy. The pylint block is vestigial — no pylint configuration or CI invocation exists — and Section 6.6 records that the test module is neither linted nor type-checked by the enforced pipeline.

### 9.4.5 Developer Tooling Pin Rationale

`requirements-dev.txt` pins exactly two of its eleven entries: `black==20.8b1` and `click==8.0.4`. Section 3.6 records the pins and notes that the `black` pin is load-bearing because formatting output changes between releases; the reason the *second* pin exists is external to the repository. Releases of `black` earlier than 22.3.0 import a private `click` symbol (`_unicodefun`) that <cite index="1-1">click 8.1.0 removed, and the published remedies were to move to Black 22.3.0 or newer, or to pin Click to 8.0.0 through 8.0.4</cite>. <cite index="6-14,6-15">The incompatibility was fixed in Black 22.3.0; earlier versions do not work with click 8.1.0.</cite>

The repository implements the second remedy exactly: `black` remains at the beta-tagged `20.8b1` release and `click` is pinned to `8.0.4`, the highest version that still exposes the symbol. Three consequences follow for anyone maintaining the formatting gate, and all three are properties of the observed configuration rather than recommendations: the two pins must move together, since raising `click` alone breaks `tox -e format` at import time; `docs/development.rst` instructs contributors to use `black` 20.8b1 specifically, so a locally installed newer `black` will reformat files that CI then rejects; and because `black` is installed through the unpinned `-rrequirements-dev.txt` dependency set of the `format`, `docs` and `setuppy` environments, the pins in that file are the only thing constraining the pair.

### 9.4.6 External References Embedded in the Source

The library records its own design lineage in code rather than only in prose. The module docstring of `schedule/__init__.py` carries three numbered citations — Adam Wiggins' "Rethinking Cron" article, the `clockwork` Ruby module repository, and the follow-up "Replace cron with clockwork" article — which are the same attributions `README.rst` and `docs/index.rst` repeat and which Section 1.2.1.1 cites as market-lineage evidence. Two transcription defects exist in that material and are recorded for accuracy: the docstring spells the author's forename "Addam", and the README feature list reads "Tested on Python and 3.7, …". Neither affects behaviour; both are reproduced verbatim into the PyPI long description and the published documentation, since `setup.py` reads `README.rst` as `long_description` and autodoc renders the docstring into the reference page.


## 9.5 Glossary

The definitions below fix the meaning of terms as this specification uses them for the `schedule` library. Where a term names an artifact in the code, the definition states the artifact; where a term is conventional, the definition states the sense in which the repository actually exercises it. Terms whose meaning is entirely generic are omitted.

### 9.5.1 Scheduling Domain Terms

| Term | Definition as used in this specification |
|---|---|
| Job | A single `Job` instance: one bound callable plus the cadence, anchor, deadline and tags that determine when it runs |
| Scheduler | A `Scheduler` instance — simultaneously the factory that creates jobs, the registry that holds them, and the synchronous executor that runs them |
| Registry | The `List[Job]` held on a scheduler instance; the entirety of the system's mutable state |
| Default scheduler | The module-level `Scheduler` created at import, against which every module-level shortcut function delegates |
| Module facade | The eight module-level shortcut functions plus the `repeat` decorator factory that forward to the default scheduler |
| Interval and unit | The numeric quantity passed to `every()` and the time unit selected by the property that follows it (seconds through weeks) |
| Cadence | The interval-plus-unit pair, informally; the recurrence rate of a job |
| Clock anchor | The `at_time` value fixed by `at()`, which pins a job to a wall-clock time within its unit |
| Start day | The weekday restriction set by a weekday property; valid only for weekly jobs |
| Deadline | The `cancel_after` instant set by `until()`, after which the job unschedules itself instead of running |
| Randomized interval (jitter) | The inclusive range produced by `every(A).to(B)`, resolved per occurrence with `random.randint` |
| Sentinel | The `CancelJob` class, returned by a job body (as the class or an instance) to request its own removal |
| Tag | Any hashable value attached to a job, used to filter retrieval, next-run queries and clearing |
| Poll cycle | One `run_pending()` invocation: scan the registry, select due jobs, execute them in next-run order |
| Due job | A job whose `should_run` is true, i.e. whose `next_run` is at or before the current instant |
| Forced sweep | A `run_all()` invocation, which executes every registered job regardless of due state |
| Missed run | An occurrence whose moment passed without a poll; the library intentionally executes it once rather than replaying each missed occurrence |
| Idle seconds | The seconds remaining until the earliest `next_run`, or `None` when nothing is scheduled |
| Serial execution | The library's only execution mode: job bodies run in-line, one after another, on the thread that called the poll |
| In-process scheduler | A scheduler that runs inside the consumer's own process with no daemon, service or separate runtime |
| Host application | The consumer program that imports the library, owns the poll loop, and supplies the job callables |
| Unschedule | Removal of a job from the registry, whether by `cancel_job()`, by `clear()`, by returning the sentinel, or by passing a deadline |

### 9.5.2 Implementation and Design Terms

| Term | Definition as used in this specification |
|---|---|
| Builder pattern | The configuration style named in the module docstring: `every()` returns an unconfigured job that successive accessors mutate |
| Fluent interface | The chained-property expression of that pattern, in which each accessor mutates `self` and returns `self` (or a related object) so the call reads as a sentence |
| Deferred registration | The property that a job joins the registry only when `do()` binds a callable, so an abandoned chain leaves no trace |
| Fail-fast validation | Rejection of an invalid declaration at definition time, by raising, rather than at execution time |
| Exception hierarchy | `ScheduleError` as the base, `ScheduleValueError` beneath it, and `IntervalError` beneath that |
| Naive datetime contract | The published guarantee that `next_run` and `last_run` carry no `tzinfo` and are expressed in the host's local time |
| Wall-clock fixation | Preserving the requested local clock reading across a UTC-offset change, rather than preserving the elapsed interval |
| Lazy optional import | Importing `pytz` inside `at()` only when a timezone is requested, which is what permits an empty required-dependency list |
| Private helper | A module-level or method-level function prefixed with `_`, excluded from the fluent API and from the published reference |
| Alias semantics | The property that the module-level `jobs` name refers to the same list object the default scheduler mutates in place, so clears remain visible through it |

### 9.5.3 Time and Timezone Terms

| Term | Definition as used in this specification |
|---|---|
| Naive datetime | A `datetime` with no `tzinfo`; interpreted as the host's local time throughout this library |
| Aware datetime | A `datetime` carrying `tzinfo`; used only inside timezone-aware next-run arithmetic and converted away before storage |
| IANA timezone | A region-based zone identifier such as `Europe/Berlin`, resolved through `pytz` when passed to `at()` |
| POSIX `TZ` string | A C-library timezone expression such as `CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3`, used by the test suite to pin the process timezone deterministically |
| UTC offset | The signed difference between a zone's local time and UTC at a given instant; may change with DST and may be non-integral in hours |
| DST | Daylight Saving Time; a scheduled change of a zone's UTC offset |
| DST gap | The interval of local time that does not exist when clocks move forward; a requested anchor inside it is scheduled one offset later as a documented best effort |
| Fold | The `datetime` attribute that disambiguates a repeated local time when clocks move backward; controlled explicitly by the test harness |
| Spring-forward and fall-back | The forward and backward offset transitions, respectively |
| Normalization | The `pytz` operation that resolves an arithmetic result to the correct offset for its instant |

### 9.5.4 Verification, Packaging and Tooling Terms

| Term | Definition as used in this specification |
|---|---|
| Quality gate | A command whose non-zero exit blocks the build; the five in this project are tests, types, documentation, formatting and packaging metadata |
| Environment matrix | The set of tox environments produced by combining interpreter versions with the optional-dependency factor |
| Factor | A tox environment-name component (here `-pytz`) that conditionally adds a dependency |
| Frozen clock | The state established by the suite's `mock_datetime` context manager, in which `datetime.datetime` returns a fixed instant |
| Skip guard | A conditional `skipTest` that converts a missing optional dependency into a skipped test rather than a failure |
| White-box test | A test that exercises a private helper directly rather than through the public API |
| Issue-numbered regression | A test whose name embeds the upstream report number it permanently pins |
| Term-missing report | The coverage output format that lists uncovered line numbers alongside the percentage |
| sdist and wheel | The source distribution (`.tar.gz`) and the built distribution (`.whl`) published to the index |
| Universal wheel | A single built distribution valid for every platform and, historically, for both Python 2 and 3 |
| Trove classifier | A standardised metadata string that categorises the distribution on PyPI |
| Extra | A named optional dependency group, installed as `schedule[timezone]` |
| Dynamic metadata | Packaging fields declared in `pyproject.toml` as supplied elsewhere, here delegated to `setup.py` |
| Inline typing marker | The `py.typed` file that tells type checkers the installed package's annotations are authoritative |
| Warnings-as-errors | The `sphinx-build -W` policy under which any documentation warning fails the build |
| Builder | A Sphinx output format target, such as `html`, `man` or `linkcheck` |
| Autodoc | The Sphinx extension that generates reference pages from docstrings in the imported package |
| Toctree | The Sphinx directive that declares navigation order and depth |
| Vendoring | Copying the single implementation file into a consumer's own tree instead of installing the distribution |
| Vestigial configuration | A setting or dependency retained in the tree that no current command exercises |


## 9.6 Acronyms

Every acronym and initialism used in this specification is expanded below, grouped by domain. Where an acronym has more than one common expansion, the third column fixes the sense in which this document uses it.

### 9.6.1 Python and Packaging Ecosystem

| Acronym | Expansion | Sense used here |
|---|---|---|
| API | Application Programming Interface | The set of Python callables the library exports; no network interface is implied |
| AST | Abstract Syntax Tree | The parsed representation used to measure the test suite's structure |
| AUR | Arch User Repository | The unmaintained downstream channel offering `python-schedule` |
| EOL | End of Life | An interpreter version no longer receiving upstream support |
| IDE | Integrated Development Environment | Editor tooling referenced by the FAQ and by the `.gitignore` JetBrains group |
| LTS | Long-Term Support | Ubuntu release class named in the outdated-package warning |
| MIT | Massachusetts Institute of Technology | Solely as the name of the licence granted by `LICENSE.txt` |
| OSI | Open Source Initiative | The body named by the `License :: OSI Approved` classifier |
| PEP | Python Enhancement Proposal | Referenced for 517/518 (build backends), 561 (inline typing) and 621 (project metadata) |
| PyPI | Python Package Index | The production publication target; TestPyPI is its staging counterpart |
| ORM | Object-Relational Mapping | Named only to record its absence from the repository |
| DDL | Data Definition Language | Named only to record its absence from the repository |

### 9.6.2 Time, Timezone and Platform

| Acronym | Expansion | Sense used here |
|---|---|---|
| DST | Daylight Saving Time | The offset transitions that dominate the library's defect and test history |
| IANA | Internet Assigned Numbers Authority | Publisher of the region-based timezone database resolved through `pytz` |
| POSIX | Portable Operating System Interface | The standard whose `TZ` string format and `tzset()` call the test suite relies on |
| TZ | Timezone (environment variable) | The process-level variable the suite pins and restores |
| UTC | Coordinated Universal Time | The reference against which zone offsets are expressed |
| CET / CEST | Central European Time / Central European Summer Time | The standard and summer designations in the pinned Berlin rule |
| NZST / NZDT | New Zealand Standard Time / New Zealand Daylight Time | The designations in the Auckland test rule |
| OS | Operating System | Used in the `Operating System :: OS Independent` classifier and in platform discussion |
| CPU | Central Processing Unit | The compute dimension in resource measurements |

### 9.6.3 Engineering Process and Quality

| Acronym | Expansion | Sense used here |
|---|---|---|
| CI | Continuous Integration | The GitHub Actions workflow named "Tests" |
| CD | Continuous Delivery / Deployment | Named to record that publication is manual, not continuous |
| PR | Pull Request | A GitHub change proposal; also a CI trigger restricted to `master` |
| VCS | Version Control System | Git, as the source of record and the boundary of what is tracked |
| SCM | Source Code Management | Synonym for the version-control plane in infrastructure diagrams |
| IaC | Infrastructure as Code | Named to record its absence; the tox and workflow files are the nearest analogue |
| SLA | Service Level Agreement | Named to record that the project publishes none |
| KPI | Key Performance Indicator | Measurable project indicators derived from the repository, not business targets |
| RPO / RTO | Recovery Point Objective / Recovery Time Objective | Continuity measures the project does not define for itself |
| QA | Quality Assurance | The gating function performed by the five CI gates |
| SAST | Static Application Security Testing | Named to record that no such scanner is configured |
| E2E | End-to-End | The absent test tier whose role in-process scenario tests occupy |
| UI | User Interface | Named to record that the system has none |
| SHA | Secure Hash Algorithm | A commit identifier, contrasted with the mutable action tags in use |
| RSS | Resident Set Size | Peak process memory in resource measurements — not syndication |

### 9.6.4 Protocols, Formats, Services and Units

| Acronym | Expansion | Sense used here |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP | HyperText Transfer Protocol | Named to record that the library performs no HTTP traffic |
| RPC | Remote Procedure Call | Named to record the absence of a remote interface |
| IPC | Inter-Process Communication | Named to record the absence of a process boundary |
| URL | Uniform Resource Locator | The declared project links in packaging metadata |
| CDN | Content Delivery Network | Named to record that no distribution edge is configured |
| SaaS | Software as a Service | The consumption model for GitHub, PyPI, Read the Docs and Coveralls |
| RTD | Read the Docs | The documentation host configured outside the repository |
| reST / RST | reStructuredText | The markup of all documentation pages and of the PyPI long description |
| HTML | HyperText Markup Language | The gated documentation output, and the sidebar template's format |

| YAML | YAML Ain't Markup Language | The CI workflow file format; the only YAML in the repository |

| KiB / MiB | Kibibyte / Mebibyte | Binary-prefix units used in artifact and memory measurements |
